title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

baseProblem.statement: Given a sorted array that has been rotated at some unknown pivot (no duplicates), find the minimum element in O(log n) time.

rounds.question: What single comparison tells you which half of the array contains the minimum?
rounds.explanation: If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is in the right half (the drop is on that side). Otherwise it's in the left half including mid.

rounds.question: What's the loop's termination condition?
options: left < right — stop when pointers meet
left <= right — stop when pointers cross
nums[left] < nums[right] — stop when the range is sorted
rounds.explanation: When left and right meet, they both point at the minimum. Using <= overshoots and breaks the invariant.

rounds.question: What's the time complexity?
rounds.explanation: Standard binary search depth. The decision at each step is O(1).

rounds.question: What if the array isn't rotated at all (e.g., [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])?
options: The algorithm fails — needs a separate code path
The algorithm works correctly because the comparison naturally directs left every iteration
You must detect this case first by checking if nums[0] < nums[n-1]
You must return nums[0] without entering the loop
rounds.explanation: An unrotated array is a rotation by zero. nums[mid] <= nums[right] holds throughout, so the search naturally walks left until pointers meet at index 0.

rounds.question: Which input most clearly tests whether your comparison choice is correct?
rounds.explanation: Implementations that compare to nums[left] instead of nums[right] return the wrong answer here. Smallest case that distinguishes correct from incorrect logic.
